title: A 2007 Version of RuneScape Won a BAFTA in 2019
hook: A version of RuneScape frozen in 2007 beat Fortnite and Pokemon Go to win the first BAFTA Mobile Game of the Year in 2019, six months after it hit phones. Do you play Old School on mobile or PC?
script: Did you know a version of RuneScape frozen in 2007 won a BAFTA in 2019? Old School RuneScape is built on the game as it existed back in 2007. For years it lived only on desktop computers. Then on October thirtieth, 2018, Jagex released it on iPhone and Android. It was the full game, not a spin-off, and your account worked on both phone and PC. The response was huge. The iPhone version was downloaded more than one million times in its first twenty-four hours. It became the number one app in eight countries that same day. By January 2019, Jagex said the mobile versions had passed five million installs. Then came the awards. In April 2019, BAFTA added a new category called Mobile Game of the Year, with the winner chosen by a public vote. The other nominees were Fortnite, Pokemon Go, Clash Royale, Brawl Stars and Roblox. Old School RuneScape beat every one of them. So a game that looks like 2007 took home a BAFTA against the biggest mobile hits on the planet. Not bad for a game that players once had to vote back into existence. Do you play Old School on your phone or on PC? Follow for more gaming history.
